samples.claim: Version test admits empty v0, rejects v2 NotSupported with value, and rejects tagged transition in v0 as CorruptFile requiring version1. Parameterized async legacy equivalence has inline/external cases; helper converts ordered mapping through legacy Group into FragReuseGroup. This is current-source legacy serializer comparison, not a released historical fixture.
samples.review_note: Version0 empty acceptance, version2 NotSupported, and tagged-v0 CorruptFile assertions match. Fresh helper reads confirm partition/history encoding and assert_corrupt variant/message checks; legacy closure converts current generated metadata rather than using a historical fixture.

samples.claim: get_or_insert takes pinned boxed Send loader future with caller lifetime. capacity==0 directly awaits each caller loader, discards returned size, returns(entry,false), preserving original error and bypassing Moka shared initialization. Thus a disabled pending load cannot force another caller to wait through this wrapper path.
samples.review_note: Capacity zero directly awaits caller loader, discards weight and returns false; pinned Send lifetime and original error propagation match. No wrapper coalescing on this branch.

samples.claim: find_ids allocates one match Vec per segment and cycles segment enumeration. Despite the optimization comment, each input ID always scans exactly all segments because there is no break after a match; the iterator returns to its initial position for the next input. It first checks segment.range then segment.position, recording each matching local ordinal, including repeated requests and IDs present in multiple segments. Missing IDs are ignored. It sorts every segment match list but does not deduplicate.
samples.review_note: The while loop performs exactly segment count steps per input and never breaks on match. Each match appends local offset; sorting lacks deduplication. Missing inputs add nothing.

samples.claim: With current tagged entry, appends_transitions returns AppendsTransitions before migration check and without inspecting groups, rewritten indices or assembly payload. Comments introduce separate uncovered rewrite escape: existing bitmap provenance must be unaffected, unknown/future histories are conservative, oversized fragment IDs cannot appear in u32 bitmaps. Comments say empty rewrites refused; actual check below only requires outer groups Vec nonempty.
samples.evidence:
113 |     // The history's own maintenance operation.
114 |     if appends_transitions {
115 |         return Ok(Admission::AppendsTransitions);
116 |     }
117 | 
118 |     // A rewrite that carries neither an entry nor transition intent is still
119 |     // safe when no current index, the entry included (its bitmap holds the
120 |     // recorded lineage), covers any rewritten fragment: it cannot invalidate
121 |     // stored provenance or the lineage, and bitmap maintenance is a no-op for
122 |     // fragments no bitmap contains. Deferred compaction of never-covered data
123 |     // commits this shape instead of growing the history with untrimmable
124 |     // transitions. Fragment ids beyond the row-address range can never appear
125 |     // in an index bitmap, so they are uncovered by definition. Only histories
126 |     // this writer understands (index_version 1) qualify: a future entry
127 |     // version may change what its bitmap means. Empty rewrites stay refused.
samples.review_note: Fresh surrounding classify branches confirm tagged-entry gating, early appends return and nonempty outer groups requirement. The annotation distinguishes explanatory comments from actual checks.

samples.claim: Four From<versions::v2_x::Writer> implementations allocate one Box and construct exactly the corresponding FileWriter variant. They consume initialized/lazy concrete writer unchanged, without validation or IO.

samples.claim: Input checks use one four-row block and assert errors for wrong values length, out-of-range position, live label9 for m2, invalid sweep block1 and advance label9. Although a comment calls an out-of-range data label corruption, check_label actually returns InvalidInput (rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:306-314). Short validity buffers, overflow and extra sweep input are not tested here; module ends.
samples.review_note: The five error assertions use the stated small block and inputs. Fresh check_label confirms InvalidInput despite corruption wording in test comment.

samples.claim: Partial-refresh fixture creates10,000 alternating single-row runs inline, updates only final offset to3, then asserts length and first two/last two values. Despite test name streams, implementation materializes the per-row vector. This is a correctness fixture, not timing/memory measurement; source tests were not executed.
samples.review_note: All 10000 alternating runs and edge-position assertions match. Fresh production refresh helper explicitly allocates and expands base_versions, so the streams test name does not prove streaming memory behavior.

samples.claim: The index-repair test confirms the row still points to an existing staging object, then resolves the version to trigger helping. It asserts canonical returned path/ETag, repaired external path/size, indexed ETag None, and NotFound for the formerly retained staging object. Thus it covers success after repair failure and eventual cleanup, without treating repair failure as rollback.
samples.review_note: Fresh fixture prefix confirms one-shot external publication failure followed by successful canonical commit. Sample checks staging retention, helping repair, canonical ETag, cleared indexed ETag and staging NotFound.

samples.claim: holes_segment filters local offsets with hash_byte %100 < holes_pct, casts them to u32, emits little-endian four-byte offsets and constructs protobuf RangeWithHoles with U32Array base=start. Iteration keeps holes sorted. range_segment builds a plain protobuf half-open Range. Neither validates arbitrary caller bounds/span against u32, relying on fixed benchmark sizes.
samples.review_note: Offset filter, u32 cast, little-endian serialization, U32Array base and half-open range match; no arbitrary-bounds validation appears.

samples.claim: Range checks only end<=sequence.len as usize then slices start,end-start. Ranges sums lengths with unchecked subtraction/casts, preallocates full requested count before per-range end checks, then slices/extends in supplied order. Neither rejects reverse bounds explicitly; arithmetic/panics can precede an InvalidInput. Error offset casts end to u32 and can truncate diagnostic values. A zero-length range accepted by end check uses slice empty shortcut.
samples.review_note: End-only checks, preallocation order, unchecked subtraction/casts and diagnostic narrowing match. Fresh slice prefix confirms zero-length shortcut.

samples.claim: String test explicitly calls AsBytes::as_bytes on str hello and expects its UTF-8 bytes; byte-slice test retains[1,2,3,4,5]. Neither tests Unicode normalization or owned String generic inference.
samples.review_note: Exact hello bytes and five-byte slice assertions match; no normalization or generic owned-String fixture.

samples.claim: IO constants: TRACE_IO_EVENTS="lance::io_events"; IO_TYPE_OPEN_SCALAR="open_scalar_index", VECTOR="open_vector_index", FRAG_REUSE="open_frag_reuse_index", MEM_WAL="open_mem_wal_index"; IO_TYPE_LOAD_VECTOR_PART="load_vector_part", SCALAR_PART="load_scalar_part". samples.claim: offset_at(position) rejects position>=total present, counts preceding runs and returns position+missing_before(k). It is inverse of position for present offsets under validated state; empty/all-missing spans return None for every input. No Result/error for out-of-range lookup.
samples.review_note: Fresh present_len/missing_before/position/runs_before_position helpers support ordinal inverse under validated run invariants. Out-of-range returns None.

samples.claim: Iterator::next advances by at most one run when remaining count is0, returning None if beyond the list; otherwise it loads that run, saturating-decrements count and returns the version even if the loaded run is empty. Thus [length1/version7,length0/version9] expands to [7,9], a source-derived counterexample not executed here. Consecutive empty runs can likewise emit phantom values. This differs from cursor/version_at, which skip empty spans.
samples.review_note: Fresh constructor/advance_run, cursor loop and version_at confirm one-step iterator advance and empty-run phantom-value deduction; cursor/random access skip empty spans. No source test was executed.

Everything else becomes Cloned(original.to_string()). Constructors generate new diagnostics rather than copying original Location/backtrace.
